title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Sources: Jensen Huang had planned to pull back Nvidia's aggressive financing and told neoclouds to get upfront customer payments; Colette Kress may go further (Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Thursday, with CFO Colette Kress appointed as interim CEO. The departure follows reports of personal misconduct involving investigations into potential diversion of restricted Nvidia chips to China via Southeast Asian partners.

items.title: Mount Thor, which is building cloud infrastructure for agentic AI on Apple silicon, raised $45M in a seed round and a Series A co-led by CRV and Conviction (Bradley C/9to5Mac)
items.content_text: Mount Thor has raised $45 million in seed and Series A funding, co-led by CRV and Conviction. The startup provides cloud-scale compute instances running macOS on Apple Silicon, specifically targeting developers needing specialized environments for agentic AI training and software testing.

items.title: Toronto-based Blue J, which provides AI-powered tax research software, raised a $176M Series E round led by JMI Equity at a $700M+ valuation (Alex Riehl/BetaKit)
items.content_text: Toronto-based AI tax research provider Blue J has secured $176 million in Series E funding led by JMI Equity, pushing its valuation past $700 million. Including secondary capital, the funding will scale the firm's agentic 'Workflows' platform and facilitate expansion into the UK market.

items.title: SK Hynix and the Korean government plan to partner on building Trinity Fab, a new $654M chip testing facility letting suppliers test products on 12-inch wafers (Yoolim Lee/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: SK Hynix and the South Korean government are investing approximately $654 million to launch the 'Trinity Fab,' a semiconductor testing facility scheduled for operation next year. The initiative provides local material, component, and equipment suppliers with a 12-inch wafer testing environment, supported by a 2 trillion KRW (approx. $1.5 billion) guarantee program to lower entry barriers into the semiconductor supply chain.

items.title: SK Hynix says it plans to spend ~$1.05B over five years to support domestic suppliers of chip materials, parts, and equipment, strengthening its supply chain (Heekyong Yang/Reuters)
items.content_text: --> South Korean company SK Hynix plans to allocate 1.4 trillion won, or $1.05 billion, over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of materials, components and equipment for semiconductor production. The program is intended to strengthen the company’s supply chain amid intensifying competition in the market for artificial intelligence chips, Channel NewsAsia reports. items.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
items.content_text: Apple, in collaboration with OpenEvidence, has launched the 'Apple Health AI Usage Study' to evaluate the accuracy and interaction efficacy of conversational AI in medical contexts. The study requires participants aged 21 and older in the US to assess AI responses via a dedicated iOS app, with an option to sync Apple HealthKit data for improved contextual relevance.

items.title: How Samsung aims to be a one-stop shop that builds, runs, and powers data centers; sources: its IT arm is in early talks to sign Anthropic and OpenAI as tenants (Financial Times)
items.content_text: Samsung Electronics is aggressively expanding its AI infrastructure ecosystem through its IT subsidiary, covering construction, operation, and power supply for data centers. The company is currently in early-stage talks with OpenAI and Anthropic to leverage its semiconductor manufacturing and hardware integration advantages for providing a one-stop AI computing solution.

items.title: Sources: Anthropic's IPO is ~7x oversubscribed; Anthropic and some of its backers are seeking to raise up to $90.4B via the IPO and a separate private placement (Bloomberg)
items.content_text: AI startup Anthropic has officially initiated its IPO process, aiming to raise $90.4 billion through a combination of an initial public offering and a concurrent private placement. The deal is currently oversubscribed by 7 times, with the company targeting a fully diluted valuation of $1.4 trillion, marking one of the largest capital raises in AI history.

items.title: Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites after ULA's Vulcan rocket fails 10 minutes into flight, marking the first mission failure for the Boeing-Lockheed joint venture (Joey Roulette/Reuters)
items.content_text: United Launch Alliance (ULA), a joint venture between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, suffered its first mission failure after its flagship Vulcan rocket experienced an anomaly 10 minutes into flight, destroying 40 Amazon Project Kuiper low-Earth orbit satellites. The incident, occurring at Space Launch Complex 41 in Florida, halts the launch cadence for Amazon's nascent satellite internet constellation.

items.title: Analysis: Huawei's Horinger data center, among China's largest for AI, has ~7% of the compute of SpaceX's Colossus 2 and may stay far behind until at least 2028 (Ben Cottier/Epoch AI)
items.content_text: Epoch AI analysis reveals that Huawei's Horinger AI data center cluster holds approximately 7% of the total compute capacity of SpaceX's Colossus 2. Driven by constraints in advanced process node chip procurement and manufacturing capacity, this infrastructure is unlikely to bridge the scale gap with global leading clusters before 2028.

items.title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
items.content_text: Nathaniel Craig, head of the particle theory group at UC Santa Barbara, utilized OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to develop a candidate nonperturbative definition of the Standard Model on a spacetime lattice. The AI acted as a core collaborator, transforming theoretical strategies into formal constructions and leading the development of complex mathematical proofs.

items.title: Our new blog for science
items.content_text: OpenAI has launched a dedicated science blog to showcase AI's cross-disciplinary research capabilities. Key milestones include addressing the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem, advancing estimates for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, and utilizing the GPT-Rosalind model in collaboration with PerturbAI and Scripps Research to analyze millions of mouse brain cells in just 32 minutes.

items.title: Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama
items.content_text: The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The latest edition of our Stepback newsletter should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning. That includes rumors that Jensen Huang might be trying to find a path back to CEO, […]

items.title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in August 2025 and has no current role, and that it runs a "legitimate and lawful business" as it opens an internal probe (Associated Press)
items.content_text: Singapore-based Megaspeed announced that executive Alice Huang left the company on August 30, 2025, and has retained external legal counsel to investigate allegations of illicitly diverting advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese firms. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent emphasized that the probe will focus on whether Nvidia fostered a culture of compliance or prioritized revenue growth over adherence to export restrictions.

items.title: Sources: Jensen Huang has discussed a comeback as Nvidia CEO with confidants, as allies form a "war room" to lobby for his return and seek White House support (Financial Times)
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated in London that the US and China must engage in dialogue and collaboration to ensure AI safety, despite its potential risks. This position aligns with discussions between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng regarding a national security-level AI communication channel, aiming to establish risk management frameworks amidst global competition.

items.title: Sources: Jensen Huang has discussed a comeback as Nvidia CEO with confidants, as allies form a "war room" to lobby for his return and seek White House support (Financial Times)
items.content_text: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is attempting to orchestrate a return to the company with support from Silicon Valley allies. However, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has publicly opposed the move, demanding that Nvidia’s board provide a detailed compliance report within 10 days regarding alleged illicit sales to Singapore-based entity Megaspeed.

items.title: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
items.content_text: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott have demanded that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify regarding chip export leakages. Legislatively, Congress is reviving the Remote Access Security Act, with House Speaker Mike Johnson confirming a growing bipartisan consensus to further restrict Nvidia's high-end chip exports to China.

items.title: Sources: Nvidia appealed to Taiwanese officials after its manager was charged over chip smuggling, and sought advice from TSMC, which declined to get involved (Mackenzie Hawkins/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs plans to add AI servers and advanced semiconductors to its export control list, making unlicensed shipments to mainland China a criminal offense under the Foreign Trade Act. This move aims to fulfill trade security commitments made to Washington, closing legal loopholes that previously forced prosecutors to rely on breach of trust or document forgery charges.

items.title: The US and Pax Silica allies, including Japan, the UK, and India, agree to create a joint list of AI technologies and supply chains to protect from China (Financial Times)
items.content_text: The United States is collaborating with Japan, the UK, and India to develop a joint list of AI technologies and supply chains to restrict China's access. This initiative marks a strategic shift in multilateral export controls, extending from traditional semiconductor hardware to AI model architectures, algorithm libraries, and core computing infrastructure.

items.title: Sources: Howard Lutnick is expected to join Trump on Air Force One to China this week, after clashing with Scott Bessent and others over Nvidia chip curbs (Ashley Gold/Semafor)
items.content_text: Howard Lutnick is expected to travel on Air Force One with the president to China this week as the commerce secretary fights to regain his footing after clashing with Trump officials over Nvidia and China chip controls, according to people familiar with the matter. items.title: Sources: Apple plans to unveil smart glasses at WWDC and ship them by the end of 2027, focusing heavily on integration of third-party iPhone apps with Siri AI (Mark Gurman/Bloomberg)

items.title: Investigation: Howard Lutnick pushed to narrow chip curbs affecting a client of his former firm Cantor Fitzgerald whose Malaysia data center may serve Tencent (New York Times)
items.content_text: U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick is advocating for less stringent export controls on AI chips destined for Southeast Asian data centers, specifically those like the A201 facility in Malaysia operated by Bitdeer, which reportedly serves Chinese tech giants. Given Lutnick's former leadership at Cantor Fitzgerald—a firm that maintains financial ties to and acts as a sales agent for these data center operators—his regulatory oversight is under scrutiny for potential conflict of interest regarding Nvidia chip export restrictions.

items.title: Scott Bessent urges Nvidia to hire an outside CEO and wants answers within 10 days on whether it pushed "seemingly illicit" chip sales to China to boost revenue (Tony Czuczka/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has formally demanded that Nvidia Corp. provide an explanation within 10 days regarding allegations of facilitating 'seemingly illicit' chip sales to China to inflate financial performance. Additionally, Bessent urged the board to hire an external CEO, signaling an intensified regulatory focus on the compliance and governance of the global AI semiconductor leader.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images, it paints them
items.content_text: Anthropic researcher Jake Eaton introduced Claude Fable 5.2, a model that bypasses traditional diffusion-based image generation by executing 1,000 to 2,000 lines of Python code. This system simulates physical brushstrokes, paint textures, and corrective layering within a virtual environment, rendering images through thousands of manually placed, coordinate-defined strokes that mimic human artistic behavior.

items.title: An overview of Jensen Huang’s messy days
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under intense scrutiny from US authorities due to a personal relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed. Alice Huang, investigated for allegedly smuggling Nvidia AI chips to China and transmitting sensitive commercial information to Beijing, had her passport confiscated by Singaporean authorities in June 2025. US intelligence is now assessing whether Jensen Huang’s proximity to this individual compromised national security or trade restriction protocols.

items.title: Inside the first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles, featuring AI announcers, lip-syncing, and human stand-ins, as the ceremony was mired in technical issues (Corbin Bolies/Variety)
items.content_text: The inaugural AI Music Awards took place in Los Angeles, hosted by the Sonic Intelligence Academy, which implemented a 'Verified Registry' to categorize entries into fully AI-generated, AI-assisted, and human-AI hybrid works. This initiative aims to establish an infrastructure comparable to the Recording Academy, seeking industry legitimacy for AI music creators amidst ongoing legal disputes over copyright infringement.

items.title: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove
items.content_text: YouTube Music (via Beyond the Beat) and Spotify are expanding AI DJ tools designed to provide background context and commentary between tracks using generative audio. However, user feedback indicates these features frequently suffer from verbose filler, mispronunciation of niche artists, and factual inconsistencies, significantly undermining the immersive streaming experience.

items.title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
items.content_text: Megaspeed, a cloud service provider, brokered approximately $12 billion worth of high-performance Nvidia AI chip orders for Chinese clients between March 2024 and June 2025. Leveraging its status as an official Nvidia cloud partner, the firm—owned by Alice Huang—facilitated the bypass of US export controls by supplying restricted silicon to Chinese tech entities through indirect channels.

items.title: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets
items.content_text: Daehwa Kim, a PhD student at Carnegie Mellon's Future Interfaces Group, presented Object Agent Twins (OATs) at the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology. The system integrates low-cost E Ink displays with sensors monitoring moisture, temperature, and motion, utilizing Google Gemini Nano to generate interactive AI avatars for physical objects.

items.title: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service
items.content_text: Mike Major, a researcher at the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), found that demand for entry-level roles in high-exposure sectors like software, customer service, and clerical work has structurally declined since late 2022. The data corroborates a global trend where AI-driven automation of repetitive tasks disproportionately hampers early-career employment, while senior-level positions remain relatively insulated.
